comment: Illustrative project policy showing how to layer project-specific rules on top of the shared defaults. A project policy fully replaces the bundled default, so the generic destructive/deploy/MCP rules are copied in at the end. Place your own version of this at <repo>/.handover/policy.json.

rules.name: handover-policy-edit
rules.reason: edit to the policy that governs your own gate — disabling rules here removes the safety net for the rest of the session. Show the user the exact change and let them approve it

rules.name: handover-policy-edit-bash
rules.reason: shell write to the policy that governs your own gate. Show the user the exact change and let them approve it

rules.name: project-no-push-main
rules.reason: This project never pushes to main directly. All work goes through a feature branch and a PR. Hand this back to the user.

rules.name: project-dangerous-script
rules.reason: reset_test_data.sql must be run manually by the user in the database console, block by block. Never run it from an agent. (Replace this pattern with whatever one-off destructive script your own project has.)

rules.name: project-db-mutations
rules.reason: Prod-adjacent database mutation. Surface the exact change to the user and get an explicit in-the-moment go-ahead. Do not retry through another tool.

rules.name: project-no-pr-merge
rules.reason: Never merge a PR yourself, against any branch. Open the PR and stop; the user merges manually. (Bare `git merge` isn't blocked here since a command string can't tell which branch is checked out, so it can't reliably distinguish merging into main from merging two feature branches.)

rules.name: destructive-git
rules.reason: Handover: destructive git operation (force-push, hard reset, clean, or branch -D). Explain what you wanted to do and hand the exact command back to the user to run.

rules.name: destructive-fs
rules.reason: Handover: recursive delete on an absolute or home path. Hand the exact command back to the user.

rules.name: destructive-sql-bash
rules.reason: Handover: destructive SQL (DROP, TRUNCATE, or DELETE without a WHERE clause). Show the user the exact statement and let them run it themselves.

rules.name: destructive-sql-mcp
rules.reason: Handover: destructive SQL (DROP, TRUNCATE, or DELETE without a WHERE clause). Show the user the exact statement and let them run it themselves.

rules.name: outward-git-ask
rules.reason: outward-facing git operation (push or PR merge)
